narr: A large upper trough shifted southeast into the Four State Region on August 21st, along the backside of an upper level low pressure system over the Great Lakes. This trough slowed as it entered the region, and interacted with rich Gulf moisture and available heating to help focus scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across the area. Given the weak steering currents aloft, these thunderstorms were slow moving and were very efficient rainfall producers, which resulted in flash flooding across the cities of Longview and Gladewater in East Texas, where widespread rainfall amounts of three to five inches fell.
ev: Several roads were flooded and closed in Longview.
Several roads flooded and closed near Gladewater.
